citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume AC. Let $M$ be an $R$-oriented boundaryless $n$-manifold, with $R$ commutative unital; manifolds are Hausdorff and second countable here. Then cap with the compatible compact orientation classes gives isomorphisms
$$D_M:H_c^p(M;R)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{n-p}(M;R)$$
for every integer $p$, including disconnected, noncompact and empty $M$.

Naturality means that for an open inclusion $i:U\hookrightarrow M$ with restricted orientation, $D_M e=i_*D_U$, where $e$ is extension of compact supports. For compact $M$, $H_c^p(M;R)=H^p(M;R)$ canonically and $D_M(a)=a\cap[M]$. For arbitrary $M$ the isomorphism is the direct sum of those on its components. AC is used in the countable coordinate-neighborhood selection for exhaustion and in the local universal-coefficient proof.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $R$ be a PID, $C$ a chain complex of free
$R$-modules, and $G$ an $R$-module. Then naturally
$$0\to\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(H_{n-1}C,G)\to H^n\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,G)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_n}\operatorname{Hom}_R(H_nC,G)\to0$$
is exact.

Let
$$0\to A^\bullet\to B^\bullet\to C^\bullet\to0$$
be a short exact sequence of cochain complexes in an abelian category. Then
there is a natural exact sequence
$$\cdots\to H^n(A)\to H^n(B)\to H^n(C)\xrightarrow{\partial^n}H^{n+1}(A)\to H^{n+1}(B)\to H^{n+1}(C)\to\cdots.$$

For every CW complex $X$, abelian group $G$, and $n\geq0$, the cellular complex has an
isomorphism $H_n^{\mathrm{cell}}(X;G)\cong H_n(X;G)$, natural with respect to
cellular maps.

Assume AC. For a CW pair $(X,A)$ and local system $\mathcal L$, the cellular cochain complex obtained from the skeletal filtration computes singular cohomology with local coefficients:
$$H^n\bigl(C^*_{\mathrm{cell}}(X,A;\mathcal L)\bigr)\cong H^n(X,A;\mathcal L).$$
For a connected pair, it is the equivariant-Hom complex on cellular chains after the published right chain action is converted to the left action $g\cdot c=c\cdot g^{-1}$; equivalently its cochains satisfy $\varphi(c\cdot g)=g^{-1}\varphi(c)$. The comparison is natural for cellular maps with correctly directed coefficient morphisms.

derivations.claim: Since $H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)$ is finite, $H^1(Y;\mathbb Q)=0$ by [F2], and $H^2(Y;\mathbb Q)=0$ by [F1]. Exactness of [F3] therefore makes $\beta:H^1(Y;\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)\to H^2(Y;\mathbb Z)$ an isomorphism. Write $\operatorname{PD}:H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)\to H^2(Y;\mathbb Z)$ for inverse cap duality.

We first fix the intersection sign and verify independence directly. For transverse oriented $2$-chains $C,T$ in an oriented $3$-manifold, orient their intersection so that $$\partial(C\cap T)=(\partial C)\cap T-C\cap(\partial T).$$ This sign follows by the outward-normal-first boundary convention in an oriented coordinate ball: taking a boundary in the second sheet passes its outward normal past the one normal direction of the first sheet. Consequently, the total signed endpoint count gives $$C\cdot\partial T=(\partial C)\cdot T.$$ These identities extend linearly to chains; the terms on paired interior faces cancel. For a closed $2$-chain $E$ and torsion cycle $y$, choose $m>0$ and $\partial T=my$. Then $m(E\cdot y)=E\cdot\partial T=0$, so $E\cdot y=0$. Thus if $\partial C=nx$ and $\partial C'=n'x$, the closed chain $n'C-nC'$ has zero intersection with $y$, giving $(C\cdot y)/n=(C'\cdot y)/n'$. Replacing $x$ by $x+\partial S$ permits replacing $C$ by $C+nS$ and changes the quotient by the integer $S\cdot y$. Replacing $y$ by $y+\partial T$ changes it by $(C\cdot\partial T)/n=x\cdot T$, also an integer. A change of transverse position is a chain homotopy: its prism has the moved-chain difference as boundary, so these same boundary identities apply. Hence the expression defines a pairing on the stated homology classes, independent of all these choices modulo $\mathbb Z$.

To identify that pairing with the Bockstein, use [F4] and [F5] and represent $x$ by a primal cellular $1$-cycle $a$, and $y$ by a dual cellular $1$-cycle $b$. Since $n[a]=0$, there is an integral primal cellular $2$-chain $C$ with $\partial C=na$. The dual-cell pairing gives the rational cellular $1$-cochain $$u(e)=\frac{C\cdot e}{n}$$ on every oriented dual edge $e$. Let $z_a$ be the integral cellular $2$-cochain on the dual complex defined by $z_a(\sigma)=a\cdot\sigma$. The sign convention in step 1.2 gives, for every dual $2$-cell $\sigma$, $$(\delta u)(\sigma)=\frac{C\cdot\partial\sigma}{n} =\frac{(\partial C)\cdot\sigma}{n} =a\cdot\sigma=z_a(\sigma).$$ There is no extra minus sign: in an oriented chart with $a$ tangent to the first coordinate and its dual $2$-cell tangent to the second and third coordinates, $a\cdot\sigma=+1$. A primal $2$-cell followed by its positive transverse dual edge likewise has intersection $+1$. These are precisely the oriented dual-cell representatives of inverse cap duality, so $[z_a]=\operatorname{PD}(x)$.

Reducing $u$ modulo $\mathbb Z$ gives a cocycle $\bar u$, because $\delta u=z_a$ is integral. Under the natural comparison [F5], the connecting map in [F3] is constructed by lifting this cocycle to a rational cochain and taking its coboundary; therefore $$\beta[\bar u]=[\delta u]=\operatorname{PD}(x),\qquad \langle[\bar u],y\rangle=u(b)\bmod\mathbb Z =\frac{C\cdot b}{n}\bmod\mathbb Z.$$ By step 1.2 this is also the bounding-chain expression for any representatives and any bounding multiple in the definition. Cellular representatives cause no restriction by [F5]: cellular and singular chain models represent the same classes, and changes of representatives and transverse positions have already been accounted for. Thus the precise identity is $$\lambda_Y(x,y)=\bigl\langle\beta^{-1}\operatorname{PD}(x),y\bigr\rangle.$$ The evaluation is on the homology class $y$, not on a cohomology class called its Poincaré dual; equivalently it is the corresponding degree-$3$ cup-product evaluation on $[Y]$.

Under [F2], evaluation identifies $H^1(Y;\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$ with the entire character group $\operatorname{Hom}(H_1(Y;\mathbb Z),\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$. The displayed identity in step 3.1 identifies the adjoint of the bounding-chain pairing with the composite of this isomorphism, $\beta^{-1}$, and $\operatorname{PD}$. All three are isomorphisms, so the pairing is nonsingular. In particular its bilinearity also follows from these homomorphisms and evaluation.

For torsion classes $x,y$, choose transverse representatives and chains $C,D$ with $\partial C=nx$ and $\partial D=my$. The boundary identity of step 1.2 applied to $C\cap D$ gives $n(x\cdot D)=m(C\cdot y)$. Interchanging a $1$-cycle and a $2$-chain in an oriented $3$-manifold changes the intersection sign by $(-1)^{(3-1)(3-2)}=+1$, so $x\cdot D=D\cdot x$. Divide by $nm$ and reduce modulo $\mathbb Z$ to obtain $\lambda_Y(x,y)=\lambda_Y(y,x)$. This proves symmetry with the signed bounding-chain convention of the definition.

citations.quote: Let $X$ be a path-connected CW space. The oriented bordism set $\Omega_n^{SO}(X)$ consists of classes of pairs $(M,f)$, where $M$ is a closed smooth oriented $n$-manifold and $f:M\to X$. Two pairs are bordant when there is a compact oriented $(n+1)$-manifold $W$ with $\partial W=M_0\sqcup(-M_1)$ and a map $F:W\to X$ restricting to $f_0$ and $f_1$ on the boundary. Disjoint union defines the operation. For a group $G$, $K(G,1)$ denotes a connected CW space with fundamental group $G$ and contractible universal cover.

derivations.claim: The sum is well-defined: if $F_i:W_i\to X$ are bordisms witnessing equivalences of pairs for $i=0,1$, then $W_0\sqcup W_1$ with map $F_0\sqcup F_1$ is a bordism witnessing the equivalence of the disjoint unions. Boundary orientations are inherited componentwise.

Disjoint union is associative and commutative up to the orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms that rebracket or permute its components; composing the maps with these diffeomorphisms preserves the bordism classes. The empty manifold with its unique map is a two-sided identity.

The cylinder $M\times[0,1]$ with map $f\circ\operatorname{pr}_M$ has boundary $(M,f)\sqcup(-M,f)$ under the product orientation convention. Thus $(-M,f)$ is a two-sided inverse of $(M,f)$, so the operation is an abelian group operation.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume AC. Let $M$ be a compact $R$-oriented $n$-manifold with boundary $A$, for a commutative unital ring $R$. Cap with its relative fundamental class gives isomorphisms, for every integer $p$,
$$S_p:H^p(M;R)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{n-p}(M,A;R),\qquad T_p:H^p(M,A;R)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{n-p}(M;R).$$
Here both maps send a class $a$ to $a\cap[M,A]$ in the displayed target. Empty boundary recovers Poincaré duality. Disconnected and empty manifolds are included. AC is inherited only from the exhaustion and local universal-coefficient arguments in Poincaré duality.

For $A\subseteq X$ there is an exact sequence
$$\cdots\to H_n(A;G)\to H_n(X;G)\to H_n(X,A;G)\xrightarrow{\delta}H_{n-1}(A;G)\to H_{n-1}(X;G)\to\cdots.$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $R$ be a PID, $C$ a chain complex of free
$R$-modules, and $G$ an $R$-module. Then naturally
$$0\to\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(H_{n-1}C,G)\to H^n\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,G)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_n}\operatorname{Hom}_R(H_nC,G)\to0$$
is exact.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every compact smooth manifold, with boundary
allowed, has the homotopy type of a finite CW complex. If its boundary is a
supplied finite CW manifold, the collar may be retained in a finite relative CW
model.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume AC. If $Y$ is a closed connected oriented $3$-manifold with finite $H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)$, then the bounding-chain torsion linking pairing $\lambda_Y$ is symmetric and nonsingular: its adjoint $H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H_1(Y;\mathbb Z),\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$ is an isomorphism.

Let $Y$ be a closed oriented $3$-manifold and let $x,y\in\operatorname{Tor}H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)$. Choose integral $1$-cycles $a,b$ representing $x,y$, respectively. For choices of an integer $n>0$ and an integral $2$-chain $C$ with $\partial C=na$, the bounding-chain expression is $(C\cdot b)/n\bmod\mathbb Z\in\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$, where $C$ and $b$ are placed transversely and intersection signs use the orientation of $Y$. This expression is the torsion linking pairing when its independence of the choices is established.

A finite nonsingular linking form is a pair $(A,\lambda)$, where $A$ is a finite abelian group and $\lambda:A\times A\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$ is symmetric and induces an isomorphism $A\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$. For $P\le A$, put $P^\perp=\{a\in A:\lambda(a,p)=0\text{ for every }p\in P\}$. A metabolizer is a subgroup $P$ with $P=P^\perp$; equivalently, $\lambda$ vanishes on $P\times P$ and $|P|^2=|A|$.

Assume AC. Let $M$ be an $R$-oriented boundaryless $n$-manifold, with $R$ commutative unital; manifolds are Hausdorff and second countable here. Then cap with the compatible compact orientation classes gives isomorphisms
$$D_M:H_c^p(M;R)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{n-p}(M;R)$$
for every integer $p$, including disconnected, noncompact and empty $M$.

Naturality means that for an open inclusion $i:U\hookrightarrow M$ with restricted orientation, $D_M e=i_*D_U$, where $e$ is extension of compact supports. For compact $M$, $H_c^p(M;R)=H^p(M;R)$ canonically and $D_M(a)=a\cap[M]$. For arbitrary $M$ the isomorphism is the direct sum of those on its components. AC is used in the countable coordinate-neighborhood selection for exhaustion and in the local universal-coefficient proof.

$$S_p:H^p(M;R)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{n-p}(M,A;R),\qquad T_p:H^p(M,A;R)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{n-p}(M;R).$$
Here both maps send a class $a$ to $a\cap[M,A]$ in the displayed target. Empty boundary recovers Poincaré duality. Disconnected and empty manifolds are included. AC is inherited only from the exhaustion and local universal-coefficient arguments in Poincaré duality.

For $\varphi\in C^p(X;R)$, $c\in C_n(X;R)$, $p,n\ge0$, over a commutative unital ring,
$$\partial(\varphi\cap c)=(-1)^p\bigl(\varphi\cap\partial c-\delta\varphi\cap c\bigr).$$
Consequently cap induces an $R$-bilinear map
$$H^p(X;R)\otimes_R H_n(X;R)\longrightarrow H_{n-p}(X;R).$$
Negative chain groups are zero, and no AC is assumed.

Let
$$0\to A^\bullet\to B^\bullet\to C^\bullet\to0$$
be a short exact sequence of cochain complexes in an abelian category. Then
there is a natural exact sequence
$$\cdots\to H^n(A)\to H^n(B)\to H^n(C)\xrightarrow{\partial^n}H^{n+1}(A)\to H^{n+1}(B)\to H^{n+1}(C)\to\cdots.$$

derivations.claim: The rational homology-pair sequence and [F1], with $H_i(W;\mathbb Q)=0$ for $i>0$, give $H_1(Y;\mathbb Q)=H_2(Y;\mathbb Q)=0$; connectedness gives $H_0(Y;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$, and orientation gives $H_3(Y;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$. Thus $Y$ is a rational homology sphere. By [F4] and [A1], both $W$ and its smooth boundary $Y$ have finite CW type, so their integral homology groups are finitely generated. The groups $H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)$, $H_1(W;\mathbb Z)$ and $H_2(W;\mathbb Z)$ have vanishing rationalizations and are therefore finite.

Put $A=H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)$, $B=H_1(W;\mathbb Z)$, and $C=H_2(W;\mathbb Z)$. Since $A$ is finite by step 1.1, the universal coefficient sequence [F3] gives $H^1(Y;\mathbb Z)=0$; [F7] then gives $H_2(Y;\mathbb Z)=0$. Also $H_3(W;\mathbb Z)=0$: [F1] identifies $H_4(W,Y)$ with $H^0(W)=\mathbb Z$, and its fundamental-class boundary maps to the generator of $H_3(Y)=\mathbb Z$; since $H_3(W,Y)\cong H^1(W)=0$, exactness forces $H_3(W)=0$.

By [F3], $H^2(W;\mathbb Z)\cong\operatorname{Ext}(B,\mathbb Z)$ and $H^3(W;\mathbb Z)\cong\operatorname{Ext}(C,\mathbb Z)$, because $B,C$ are finite and $H_3(W)=0$. Their orders are $|B|$ and $|C|$. Under [F1], these are the orders of $H_2(W,Y)$ and $H_1(W,Y)$, respectively. The pair sequence [F2] shows that $P=\ker(A\to B)$ is the cokernel of the injective map $H_2(W)\to H_2(W,Y)$, while $B\to H_1(W,Y)$ is onto because the next map $H_0(Y)\to H_0(W)$ is an isomorphism. Hence $|P|=|B|/|C|$ and $|A/P|=|B|/|C|$, so $|A|=|P|^2$.

To prove isotropy, [F2] and the naturality in [F7] identify $P$ under Poincaré duality with the image of $H^2(W;\mathbb Z)\to H^2(Y;\mathbb Z)$. For $x,y\in P$, choose lifts $\widetilde x,\widetilde y\in H^2(W;\mathbb Z)$. Since $W$ is a rational homology ball, the coefficient Bockstein $H^1(W;\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)\to H^2(W;\mathbb Z)$ is onto by [F8]: the adjacent groups $H^1(W;\mathbb Q)$ and $H^2(W;\mathbb Q)$ vanish. Choose $\gamma\in H^1(W;\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$ with Bockstein $\widetilde y$. The Bockstein–duality formula in [F5] evaluates $\lambda_Y(y,x)$ as the restriction of $\gamma\smile\widetilde x$ on $[Y]$; symmetry of $\lambda_Y$ then gives the same value for $\lambda_Y(x,y)$. This class extends over $W$, and the inclusion sends $[Y]$ to zero in $H_3(W)$ because $Y=\partial W$. Thus $\lambda_Y(x,y)=0$.
The isotropy from step 3.2 gives $P\subseteq P^\perp$. Nonsingularity [F5] implies $|P^\perp|=|A|/|P|=|P|$ by step 3.1. Therefore $P=P^\perp$, so $P$ is a metabolizer by [F6].

The positive meridian is the oriented circle $\{x\}\times\partial D^2$ in the overlap $D^2\times S^1$, oriented by the ambient and disk orientations.

For an open cover $X=U\cup V$, the sequence
$$\cdots\to H_n(U\cap V;G)\to H_n(U;G)\oplus H_n(V;G)\to H_n(X;G)\xrightarrow{\delta}H_{n-1}(U\cap V;G)\to\cdots$$

citations.quote: Let $X$ be a path-connected CW space. The oriented bordism set $\Omega_n^{SO}(X)$ consists of classes of pairs $(M,f)$, where $M$ is a closed smooth oriented $n$-manifold and $f:M\to X$. Two pairs are bordant when there is a compact oriented $(n+1)$-manifold $W$ with $\partial W=M_0\sqcup(-M_1)$ and a map $F:W\to X$ restricting to $f_0$ and $f_1$ on the boundary. Disjoint union defines the operation. For a group $G$, $K(G,1)$ denotes a connected CW space with fundamental group $G$ and contractible universal cover.

For every path-connected CW space $X$, disjoint union makes $\Omega_n^{SO}(X)$ an abelian group with identity the empty manifold with its unique map to $X$ and inverse of $(M,f)$ represented by $(-M,f)$.

Assume AC. Let $d\ge1$ and $B=K(C_d\times\mathbb Z,1)$. For geometric oriented **smooth** bordism of maps,
$$\Omega^{SO}_3(B)\cong\mathbb Z/d.$$
In degree four, forgetting the map splits the constant-map inclusion, and its kernel is a finite group isomorphic to $\mathbb Z/d$. In particular, for every closed smooth oriented four-manifold $Z$ and map $f:Z\to B$,
$$d\bigl([Z,f]-[Z,\mathrm{constant}]\bigr)=0\quad\hbox{in }\Omega^{SO}_4(B).$$
Thus that displayed disjoint union, with reversed orientations for its negative terms, bounds an actual compact smooth oriented five-manifold over $B$. No TOP bordism calculation or generalized-homology axiom for geometric bordism is presupposed.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume AC. Let $D\subset B^4$ be a smooth proper disk and let $X_D$ be its compact exterior. Then $X_D$ is connected, $H_1(X_D;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$ generated by the positive meridian, and $H_i(X_D;\mathbb Z)=0$ for every $i\ge2$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $R$ be a PID, $C$ a chain complex of free
right $R$-modules, and $G$ a left $R$-module. Then naturally in $C,G$,
$0\to H_n(C)\otimes_RG\to H_n(C\otimes_RG)\to\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(H_{n-1}(C),G)\to0$
is exact.

Assume AC. Let $X_D$ be the exterior of a smooth proper disk, with positive-meridian isomorphism $H_1(X_D;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$. Let $X_{D,\infty}$ be the connected cover classified by the kernel of $\pi_1(X_D)\to H_1(X_D;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$, and let $t$ denote the deck transformation represented by the positive meridian. For $q\ge2$, define $X_{D,q}=X_{D,\infty}/\langle t^q\rangle$.

Let
$$0\to A_\bullet\to B_\bullet\to C_\bullet\to0$$
be a short exact sequence of complexes in an abelian category. Then there is an
exact sequence
$$\cdots\to H_n(A)\to H_n(B)\to H_n(C)\xrightarrow{\partial_n}H_{n-1}(A)\to H_{n-1}(B)\to H_{n-1}(C)\to\cdots.$$

derivations.claim: The deck transformation acts trivially on $H_0(X_{D,\infty};\mathbb F_p)\cong\mathbb F_p$ because the cover is connected. From the first sequence in [F2], its homology exact sequence and [F1] show that $t-1$ is an isomorphism on $H_i(X_{D,\infty};\mathbb F_p)$ for every $i\ge1$: for $i\ge2$ both neighboring homology groups of $X_D$ vanish, while in degree one exactness uses $H_2(X_D)=0$, $H_1(X_D)=\mathbb F_p$, and the zero map $t-1$ on $H_0(X_{D,\infty})$. Thus the degree-one quotient and kernel both vanish.

In characteristic $p$, repeated Frobenius gives $t^{p^k}-1=(t-1)^{p^k}$. Therefore $t^q-1$ is an isomorphism on every positive-degree homology group of $X_{D,\infty}$ and is zero on its degree-zero homology. The long exact sequence of the second sequence in [F2] now gives $H_1(X_{D,q};\mathbb F_p)\cong H_0(X_{D,\infty};\mathbb F_p)\cong\mathbb F_p$, while the quotient cover is connected and hence $H_0(X_{D,q};\mathbb F_p)\cong\mathbb F_p$.

For each $i\ge2$, both the cokernel on $H_i(X_{D,\infty})$ and the kernel on $H_{i-1}(X_{D,\infty})$ of $t^q-1$ vanish by step 2.1 and the isomorphisms of step 1.1. Exactness therefore gives $H_i(X_{D,q};\mathbb F_p)=0$. This includes all higher degrees and completes the calculation.

derivations.claim: The core circle of $D^2\times S^1$ is the lift of $\mu^q$. Lift that loop to the infinite cyclic cover $X_{D,\infty}$: it is a path from a point $\widetilde x$ to $t^q\widetilde x$. The connecting map of the chain sequence for the $q$-fold quotient sends its homology class to $[\widetilde x]\in H_0(X_{D,\infty};\mathbb F_p)$. By the proof of [F2], this connecting map is an isomorphism in degree one, so the overlap map $H_1(D^2\times S^1;\mathbb F_p)\to H_1(X_{D,q};\mathbb F_p)$ is an isomorphism.

The filling piece $D^2\times D^2$ is contractible and the overlap has homology only in degrees zero and one. The Mayer–Vietoris sequence [F4], using the isomorphism from step 1.1, gives $H_i(W_{D,q};\mathbb F_p)=0$ for every $i>0$. The two glued pieces and their overlap are connected, so $W_{D,q}$ is connected; orientation is inherited from the cyclic branched covering map away from the branch set and extends over the local model.

By [F3], each integral homology group $H_i(W_{D,q};\mathbb Z)$ is finitely generated. The injection $H_i(W_{D,q};\mathbb Z)\otimes\mathbb F_p\hookrightarrow H_i(W_{D,q};\mathbb F_p)$ from [F5] makes that tensor product zero for $i>0$. A finitely generated abelian group with zero tensor product with $\mathbb F_p$ has rank zero; hence $H_i(W_{D,q};\mathbb Q)=0$. Its boundary is $\Sigma_q(\partial D)$ by [F1], proving the statement.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot and $q\ge2$. Let $S^3_0(K)$ be zero-framed Dehn surgery on $K$, filling its exterior along the preferred longitude. The exterior meridian-coordinate map to $\mathbb Z/q$ sends the preferred longitude to zero and therefore extends across this filling. Let $M_{0,q}$ be the connected $q$-fold cyclic cover classified by its kernel, and let $\widetilde\mu$ denote the closed lift of $\mu^q$, where $\mu$ is the positive meridian of $K$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented $3$-sphere, choose its compact exterior $E_K$ with boundary torus $T_K$, and let $\mu$ and $\lambda$ be its positive meridian and preferred longitude. The exterior homology theorem gives $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[\mu]$. Let $\phi:\pi_1(E_K)\to\mathbb Z$ be the composite of abelianization with the homomorphism $[\mu]\mapsto1$. For an integer $q\ge2$, let $\phi_q$ be the composite $\pi_1(E_K)\xrightarrow{\phi}\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z/q\mathbb Z$, and let $p_q:E_q\to E_K$ be the connected cover classified by $\ker\phi_q$. On $T_K$, the homomorphism sends $[\mu]\mapsto1$ and $[\lambda]\mapsto0$, so the preimage of $T_K$ is a connected torus cover whose fundamental group corresponds to $\langle\mu^q,\lambda\rangle$. Let $\widetilde\mu$ be the closed lift of $\mu^q$. Attach a solid torus to $E_q$ with its meridian identified with $\widetilde\mu$; the resulting oriented closed $3$-manifold is the $q$-fold cyclic branched cover $\Sigma_q(K)$. In tubular coordinates near $K$, the extended map to $S^3$ has local form $(s,w)\mapsto(s,w^q)$, and the deck group $\mathbb Z/q\mathbb Z$ acts by $w\mapsto e^{2\pi i/q}w$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Every smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$ bounds a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface $F\subset S^3$ whose oriented boundary is $K$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Let $L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_r\subset S^3$ be a nonempty smooth oriented link, let $F$ be a compact smooth oriented embedded surface with oriented boundary $L$, and put $X=S^3\setminus L$. If a smooth oriented loop $J\subset X$ is transverse to the interior of $F$, define its signed intersection number $J\cdot F$ by counting $+1$ when $J$ crosses from the negative to the positive side of the oriented normal of $F$ and $-1$ for the reverse crossing. Then $J\cdot F=\varphi([J])$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented $3$-sphere, choose its compact exterior $E_K$ with boundary torus $T_K$, and let $\mu$ and $\lambda$ be its positive meridian and preferred longitude. The exterior homology theorem gives $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[\mu]$. Let $\phi:\pi_1(E_K)\to\mathbb Z$ be the composite of abelianization with the homomorphism $[\mu]\mapsto1$. For an integer $q\ge2$, let $\phi_q$ be the composite $\pi_1(E_K)\xrightarrow{\phi}\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z/q\mathbb Z$, and let $p_q:E_q\to E_K$ be the connected cover classified by $\ker\phi_q$. On $T_K$, the homomorphism sends $[\mu]\mapsto1$ and $[\lambda]\mapsto0$, so the preimage of $T_K$ is a connected torus cover whose fundamental group corresponds to $\langle\mu^q,\lambda\rangle$. Let $\widetilde\mu$ be the closed lift of $\mu^q$. Attach a solid torus to $E_q$ with its meridian identified with $\widetilde\mu$; the resulting oriented closed $3$-manifold is the $q$-fold cyclic branched cover $\Sigma_q(K)$. In tubular coordinates near $K$, the extended map to $S^3$ has local form $(s,w)\mapsto(s,w^q)$, and the deck group $\mathbb Z/q\mathbb Z$ acts by $w\mapsto e^{2\pi i/q}w$.

Let $B$ be nonempty, path-connected, locally path-connected, and semilocally simply connected, fix $b_0\in B$, and put $G=\pi_1(B,b_0)$.

1. The assignment $$[p:(E,e_0)\to(B,b_0)]\longmapsto p_*\pi_1(E,e_0)$$ is a bijection from based-isomorphism classes of based connected coverings of $B$ to subgroups of $G$.
2. After forgetting the chosen point in the fibre, the assignment to the conjugacy class of $p_*\pi_1(E,e_0)$ is a bijection from isomorphism classes of connected coverings of $B$ to conjugacy classes of subgroups of $G$.

Let $Y$ be path-connected and locally path-connected, let $f:(Y,y_0)\to(B,b_0)$ be based, and let $p:(E,e_0)\to(B,b_0)$ be a covering. A based lift $\widetilde f:(Y,y_0)\to(E,e_0)$ exists if and only if $f_*\pi_1(Y,y_0)\subseteq p_*\pi_1(E,e_0)$; when it exists it is unique.

derivations.claim: Choose a Seifert surface for $K$ by [F4] and remove its boundary collar to obtain a properly embedded surface $F_0$ in the knot exterior. Its boundary is a degree-one longitude curve, hence represents the preferred longitude by [F3]. Each element of $\pi_1(F_0)$ has a smooth loop representative. Push that loop slightly to one side of the Seifert surface; the push is homotopic in the exterior and disjoint from the surface, so [F5] gives meridian coordinate zero. Thus $\ell_K\bmod q$ vanishes on $\pi_1(F_0)$, and [F7] lifts $F_0$ to each sheet of $E_q$. Each lifted copy has one boundary component over the preferred longitude, proving that every lifted longitude is nullhomologous in $E_q$.

In the branched filling, $\widetilde\mu$ bounds the attached solid torus's meridian disk and a longitude lift maps to its core generator. The same Mayer–Vietoris cokernel calculation [F6] gives $H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)\cong H_1(E_q;\mathbb Z)/\langle[\widetilde\mu]\rangle$.

In the zero-surgery filling, the boundary-torus basis consists of the closed meridian lift $\widetilde\mu$ and a longitude lift $\widetilde\lambda$. The latter bounds a meridian disk in the attached solid torus and the former maps to its core generator. The Mayer–Vietoris cokernel in [F6] therefore eliminates the core generator and gives $H_1(M_{0,q};\mathbb Z)\cong H_1(E_q;\mathbb Z)/\langle[\widetilde\lambda]\rangle$. Step 1.1 makes this quotient $H_1(E_q;\mathbb Z)$.

The cover subgroup is $\ker(\ell_K\bmod q)$ by [F7]. Thus $\ell_K(g)$ is divisible by $q$ for every $g\in\pi_1(E_q)$, and $g\mapsto\ell_K(g)/q$ is a homomorphism $\pi_1(E_q)\to\mathbb Z$. It descends to $r:H_1(E_q;\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Z$ and satisfies $r([\widetilde\mu])=1$, since $\widetilde\mu$ projects to $\mu^q$. Therefore $\mathbb Z[\widetilde\mu]$ is a direct summand and $H_1(E_q)\cong H_1(E_q)/\langle[\widetilde\mu]\rangle\oplus\mathbb Z[\widetilde\mu]$. Using step 1.2 and then step 2.1 proves the statement.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if

Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that

Assume AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot bounding a smooth proper disk $D\subset B^4$, and let $q\ge2$. Write $X_D$ for the compact disk exterior and let the positive meridian induce $\pi_1(X_D)\to H_1(X_D;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z/q$. Let $X_{D,q}$ be the connected cover classified by the kernel of this map. Attach $D^2\times D^2$ to $X_{D,q}$ along the connected cover of $D^2\times S^1$ using the normal-disk map $z\mapsto z^q$. The resulting compact oriented $4$-manifold $W_{D,q}$ is the $q$-fold cyclic cover of $B^4$ branched along $D$; its boundary is $\Sigma_q(K)$, and the local branched model is $(x,z)\mapsto(x,z^q)$.

Assume AC. Let $D\subset B^4$ be a smooth proper disk, let $p$ be prime, and let $q=p^k$ with $k\ge1$. The $q$-fold cyclic cover $W_{D,q}$ of $B^4$ branched along $D$ is a compact connected oriented $4$-manifold with $H_i(W_{D,q};\mathbb Q)=0$ for every $i>0$ and boundary $\Sigma_q(\partial D)$.

Assume AC. Let $W$ be a compact connected smooth oriented $4$-manifold with rational homology of a point and connected boundary $Y$. Then $Y$ is a rational homology sphere, and $P=\ker(H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)\to H_1(W;\mathbb Z))$ is a metabolizer for the torsion linking form $\lambda_Y$.

Assume AC. If $Y$ is a closed connected oriented $3$-manifold with finite $H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)$, then the bounding-chain torsion linking pairing $\lambda_Y$ is symmetric and nonsingular: its adjoint $H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H_1(Y;\mathbb Z),\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$ is an isomorphism.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere and let $B^4$ be the standard four-ball with boundary $S^3$. Let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable smooth properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. Let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable locally flat topologically properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. For each such surface, its genus $g(F)$ is the nonnegative integer determined by $\chi(F)=1-2g(F)$. Define the smooth slice genus and the locally flat topological slice genus by

$$
g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K):=\min\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K),\qquad g_4^{\mathrm{top}}(K):=\min\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K).
$$

A finite nonsingular linking form is a pair $(A,\lambda)$, where $A$ is a finite abelian group and $\lambda:A\times A\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$ is symmetric and induces an isomorphism $A\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$. For $P\le A$, put $P^\perp=\{a\in A:\lambda(a,p)=0\text{ for every }p\in P\}$. A metabolizer is a subgroup $P$ with $P=P^\perp$; equivalently, $\lambda$ vanishes on $P\times P$ and $|P|^2=|A|$.

Assume AC. For every smooth oriented knot $K$ and $q\ge2$, the first homology of the $q$-fold cyclic cover $M_{0,q}$ of zero surgery has an isomorphism of abelian groups
$$H_1(M_{0,q};\mathbb Z)\cong H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)\oplus\mathbb Z,$$
where the free summand is generated by $\widetilde\mu$, the closed lift of the $q$-fold meridian loop $\mu^q$.
Assume AC, as in the smooth Casson–Gordon bordism convention. For every prime-power integer $d$ and $G=\mathbb Z/d\oplus\mathbb Z$, the oriented bordism group $\Omega_3^{SO}(K(G,1))$ is finite.

Let $X$ be a path-connected CW space. The oriented bordism set $\Omega_n^{SO}(X)$ consists of classes of pairs $(M,f)$, where $M$ is a closed smooth oriented $n$-manifold and $f:M\to X$. Two pairs are bordant when there is a compact oriented $(n+1)$-manifold $W$ with $\partial W=M_0\sqcup(-M_1)$ and a map $F:W\to X$ restricting to $f_0$ and $f_1$ on the boundary. Disjoint union defines the operation. For a group $G$, $K(G,1)$ denotes a connected CW space with fundamental group $G$ and contractible universal cover.

For every path-connected CW space $X$, disjoint union makes $\Omega_n^{SO}(X)$ an abelian group with identity the empty manifold with its unique map to $X$ and inverse of $(M,f)$ represented by $(-M,f)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice as an ambient hypothesis; the finite construction and
the ODE interfaces below use no additional choice, so this hypothesis is
dispensable. A smooth manifold with corners here is Hausdorff and second
countable, with charts in relatively open subsets of $[0,\infty)^c\times\mathbb R^{n-c}$
and transition maps smoothly extendible with invertible derivative at corner
points; transitions preserve the local depth and its face germs. Let $M$ be
compact. Then $M$ has a finite corner-adapted whole-star smooth triangulation.
Corner faces are locally subpolyhedra, and any specified finite union of
closed faces is a subpolyhedron.

If the total boundary already has a finite piecewise smooth triangulation
$f:L\to\partial M$ compatible on all local face intersections, with its
differential fan giving a homeomorphism onto the union of boundary faces of the
tangent orthant at each point, the triangulation extends to $M$, pointwise
preserving $f$ with compatible subdivisions allowed. In the resulting finite
union construction all intersections may be made full subcomplexes. The same
relative conclusion applies to a fixed corner-adapted triangulated closed neighbourhood piece
whose smaller protected subcomplex lies in its relative interior: fitting is
performed away from that protected subcomplex. No extension of arbitrary
incompatible boundary data is asserted.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: On [F1]'s branched-cover summand send a class to its character value, identifying its cyclic image with $C_d$; send $\widetilde\mu$ to zero in that factor. In the other factor use the integral free projection. This is the stated homomorphism $\eta$ on actual integral homology and hence on the fundamental group. It is represented by a continuous map to the specified $K(G,1)$: on a finite CW presentation send each one-cell to a loop with the assigned group image, fill each two-cell because its relation has trivial image, and extend over higher cells because the target's higher homotopy groups vanish. The extensions agree on cell boundaries; their finite pasting is continuous. AC permits these finite choices, and changing them alters the map only within its homotopy class by the same cell-by-cell argument.

Its geometric class belongs to [F2]'s finite group. Some positive integer $r$ kills that element (indeed the explicit calculation permits $r=d$). By [F3], zero means that the disjoint union of those $r$ actual marked copies bounds a compact smooth oriented four-manifold with a map to $K(G,1)$ restricting to their maps. This is exactly the required bordism datum, with the positive orientations and both prescribed character coordinates unchanged.

Assume AC. If a smooth oriented knot $K$ bounds a smooth proper disk $D$ in $B^4$ and $q$ is a prime power, then
$$P_D=\ker\bigl(H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)\to H_1(W_{D,q};\mathbb Z)\bigr)$$
is a metabolizer for the torsion linking form of $\Sigma_q(K)$.

Assume AC. Let $D\subset B^4$ be a smooth proper disk, let $p$ be prime, and let $q=p^k$ with $k\ge1$. The $q$-fold cyclic cover $W_{D,q}$ of $B^4$ branched along $D$ is a compact connected oriented $4$-manifold with $H_i(W_{D,q};\mathbb Q)=0$ for every $i>0$ and boundary $\Sigma_q(\partial D)$.

Assume AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $q\ge2$, and let $M=\Sigma_q(K)$ be its $q$-fold cyclic branched cover. A character is a homomorphism $\chi:H_1(M;\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$. Its order is its order in $\operatorname{Hom}(H_1(M;\mathbb Z),\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$; it is finite-order when this order is finite and has prime-power order when its order is $p^e$ for a prime $p$ and $e\ge1$. It vanishes on a subgroup $P$ when $\chi(x)=0$ for every $x\in P$.

derivations.claim: If $\chi$ extends to $\widetilde\chi:H_1(W_{D,q};\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$, then for every $x\in P_D$ one has $i(x)=0$, so $\chi(x)=\widetilde\chi(i(x))=0$. The extension has finite image because its domain is finite.

Conversely, suppose $\chi(P_D)=0$. Then $\chi$ factors uniquely through the subgroup $I=i(H_1(\Sigma_q(\partial D)))$ of the finite group $B=H_1(W_{D,q})$. Let $p$ be the prime underlying the order of $\chi$ as in [F2]. Every element of order coprime to $p$ maps to zero, since its image is killed both by a power of $p$ and by an integer coprime to $p$. Thus the factored map restricts to the $p$-primary subgroup $I_p\le B_p$.

A homomorphism from a subgroup $J$ of a finite abelian $p$-group $B_p$ into $\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z[p^\infty]$ extends when one adjoins one element $b\in B_p$: if $p^k$ is the order of $b+J$, choose $c\in\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z[p^\infty]$ with $p^kc=f(p^kb)$, which exists because multiplication by $p^k$ is surjective on this Prüfer group. Set $f'(j+rb)=f(j)+rc$. If $j+rb=j'+r'b$, then $(r-r')b\in J$, so $r-r'$ is divisible by $p^k$; the chosen equation makes the two values equal. The extension is therefore well-defined. Repeating this finite step extends the character from $I_p$ to $B_p$.

Set the extension to zero on the complementary primary summand of $B$ and combine it with the extension on $B_p$. The resulting character on $B$ extends $\chi$ and has finite $p$-power image because $B$ is finite and the values are $p$-primary. This proves the reverse implication.

citations.quote: Assume AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, $q\ge2$, and $M=\Sigma_q(K)$ oriented as the boundary of the positive-meridian branched cover. When $H_1(M;\mathbb Z)$ is finite, its torsion linking form is the oriented pairing $\lambda_M:H_1(M;\mathbb Z)\times H_1(M;\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$ given by $\lambda_M(x,y)=(C\cdot y)/n\bmod\mathbb Z$ for any integer $n>0$ and integral $2$-chain $C$ in $M$ with $\partial C=nx$; reversing the orientation negates $\lambda_M$. For a prime-power-order character $\chi$ of order $d$, the standard splitting $H_1(M_{0,q};\mathbb Z)\cong H_1(M;\mathbb Z)\oplus\mathbb Z\langle\widetilde\mu\rangle$ of the $q$-fold cyclic cover $M_{0,q}$ of zero surgery extends $\chi$ to $\eta:H_1(M_{0,q};\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Z/d\oplus\mathbb Z$ by identifying its cyclic image with $\mathbb Z/d$ and using the free-summand projection in the second factor. A Casson–Gordon bordism datum is a positive integer $r$ and a compact oriented $4$-manifold $W$ with a map to $K(\mathbb Z/d\oplus\mathbb Z,1)$ whose boundary represents $r$ copies of $(M_{0,q},\eta)$.

Assume AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $q$ be a prime power, and let $\chi:H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$ have prime-power order $d$. Under the standard splitting $H_1(M_{0,q};\mathbb Z)\cong H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)\oplus\mathbb Z\langle\widetilde\mu\rangle$, the character extends to $\eta:H_1(M_{0,q};\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Z/d\oplus\mathbb Z$ by identifying its cyclic image with $\mathbb Z/d$ and using the free-summand projection in the second factor. Some positive multiple of $(M_{0,q},\eta)$ bounds a compact oriented $4$-manifold with an extending map to $K(\mathbb Z/d\oplus\mathbb Z,1)$.

Assume AC. Let $X$ be a smooth knot exterior or the exterior of a smooth proper disk in the standard four-ball. Its meridian-coordinate homomorphism is $\ell:\pi_1X\to\mathbb Z$. Let $X_q$ be its connected $q$-fold cyclic cover, for any $q\ge1$, and put $\psi=\ell/q$ on its group. For any homomorphism $c:\pi_1X_q\to C_{p^a}$, where $p$ is prime and $a\ge1$, give $\mathbb C(t)$ the rank-one unitary coefficient system
$$\rho(g)=\zeta_{p^a}^{c(g)}t^{\psi(g)},\qquad \bar t=t^{-1}.$$
Then $H_*(X_q;\mathbb C(t)_\rho)=0$. The same conclusion holds for a trivial finite character.

If $M_{0,q}$ is the $q$-fold cover of zero surgery on a smooth knot, and $c$ is any prime-power-order character on its first homology, the same conclusion holds on $M_{0,q}$ with its meridian free coordinate. In particular every smooth four-bordism whose boundary consists of such data has a nonsingular twisted middle Hermitian form, with no change to its absolute twisted $H_2$. The regular $C_{p^a}\times\mathbb Z$ cover in this assertion is generally infinite; the assertion concerns its specified rank-one localization.

Assume AC. Let $F$ be a commutative field of characteristic different from two with involution, and supply a rank-one unitary $F$ local system on each smooth compact oriented manifold in question, with one compatible system on each gluing or bordism. Give its finite-dimensional local homology the usual Hermitian cap-intersection form.

For a four-manifold $W$, the radical of its absolute middle form is exactly the image of $H_2(\partial W;F)$; denote its nonsingular quotient form by $Q_F(W)$. If $\partial W$ is $F$-acyclic, this is the absolute middle form itself. If two four-manifolds with the same entire marked boundary are glued with opposite boundary orientations, giving a closed $Z=W_0\cup_{\partial}(-W_1)$, then
$$[Q_F(Z)]=[Q_F(W_0)]-[Q_F(W_1)]\quad\text{in }W(F).$$
The nonsingular middle form of the boundary of any compact oriented smooth five-manifold with extending coefficients is metabolic, hence zero in $W(F)$. All assertions commute with extension of involutive fields, disjoint union, orientation reversal and coefficient-compatible marked identifications. In particular, the untwisted form used for a manifold with boundary is its nonsingular image form, not an unsupported assertion that its entire ordinary $H_2$ has nonsingular intersection form.

derivations.claim: The deck group $G=C_d\times\mathbb Z$ includes an infinite cyclic factor. Thus its regular cover $Y$ is not a finite-sheeted cover: the free coordinate takes the boundary meridian to one and gives arbitrarily many different sheets. Use the regular cover and the rank-one character projection followed by Laurent-field localization specified in [F2]. Its exactness identifies the module in the Statement with $H_2(W;F)$.

By [F2], $H_i(\partial W;F)=0$ in every degree. The actual pair sequence therefore identifies $H_2(W;F)$ with $H_2(W,\partial W;F)$. By [F3] the latter is its conjugate dual, with this map exactly the intersection pairing. It follows that the pairing is nonsingular. The involution in [F2] is precisely complex conjugation with $t\mapsto t^{-1}$, so the pairing is Hermitian in the stated convention.

To spell out the boundary cap, split each finite-dimensional boundary chain group into its cycles and a complement; the differential on that complement is an isomorphism to the preceding boundary space. Its inverses give a contraction of the acyclic boundary complex. The quotient from absolute to relative chains consequently has contractible kernel and preserves the absolute middle homology. This algebraic Poincare cap is enough for the Witt construction; it changes neither its module nor its pairing. The ordinary form, which need not be nonsingular on all ordinary $H_2$, instead uses [F3]'s quotient by its boundary radical. These are distinct operations, and no nonexistent finite $G$-cover or geometric attachment preserving a singular ordinary form has been assumed.

citations.quote: Assume AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $q$ be a prime power, and let $\chi:H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$ have prime-power order $d$. Under the standard splitting $H_1(M_{0,q};\mathbb Z)\cong H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)\oplus\mathbb Z\langle\widetilde\mu\rangle$, the character extends to $\eta:H_1(M_{0,q};\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Z/d\oplus\mathbb Z$ by identifying its cyclic image with $\mathbb Z/d$ and using the free-summand projection in the second factor. Some positive multiple of $(M_{0,q},\eta)$ bounds a compact oriented $4$-manifold with an extending map to $K(\mathbb Z/d\oplus\mathbb Z,1)$.

Assume AC. Let $(W,\eta)$ be a Casson–Gordon bordism datum for a prime-power order character, and let $Y$ be its regular cover with deck action $G=\mathbb Z/d\oplus\mathbb Z$. After the boundary capping that kills the meridian-class radical, the twisted intersection form on
$$H_2(Y;\mathbb C)\otimes_{\mathbb C[G]}\mathbb C(t)$$
is a nonsingular Hermitian form for the involution $(\zeta_d,t)\mapsto(\overline{\zeta_d},t^{-1})$. The capping preserves the $H_2$ module used in the Witt-class construction.

Assume AC. Let $d\ge1$ and $B=K(C_d\times\mathbb Z,1)$. For geometric oriented **smooth** bordism of maps,
$$\Omega^{SO}_3(B)\cong\mathbb Z/d.$$
In degree four, forgetting the map splits the constant-map inclusion, and its kernel is a finite group isomorphic to $\mathbb Z/d$. In particular, for every closed smooth oriented four-manifold $Z$ and map $f:Z\to B$,
$$d\bigl([Z,f]-[Z,\mathrm{constant}]\bigr)=0\quad\hbox{in }\Omega^{SO}_4(B).$$
Thus that displayed disjoint union, with reversed orientations for its negative terms, bounds an actual compact smooth oriented five-manifold over $B$. No TOP bordism calculation or generalized-homology axiom for geometric bordism is presupposed.

Assume AC. Let $F$ be a commutative field of characteristic different from two with involution, and supply a rank-one unitary $F$ local system on each smooth compact oriented manifold in question, with one compatible system on each gluing or bordism. Give its finite-dimensional local homology the usual Hermitian cap-intersection form.

For a four-manifold $W$, the radical of its absolute middle form is exactly the image of $H_2(\partial W;F)$; denote its nonsingular quotient form by $Q_F(W)$. If $\partial W$ is $F$-acyclic, this is the absolute middle form itself. If two four-manifolds with the same entire marked boundary are glued with opposite boundary orientations, giving a closed $Z=W_0\cup_{\partial}(-W_1)$, then
$$[Q_F(Z)]=[Q_F(W_0)]-[Q_F(W_1)]\quad\text{in }W(F).$$
The nonsingular middle form of the boundary of any compact oriented smooth five-manifold with extending coefficients is metabolic, hence zero in $W(F)$. All assertions commute with extension of involutive fields, disjoint union, orientation reversal and coefficient-compatible marked identifications. In particular, the untwisted form used for a manifold with boundary is its nonsingular image form, not an unsupported assertion that its entire ordinary $H_2$ has nonsingular intersection form.

Let $X$ be a path-connected CW space. The oriented bordism set $\Omega_n^{SO}(X)$ consists of classes of pairs $(M,f)$, where $M$ is a closed smooth oriented $n$-manifold and $f:M\to X$. Two pairs are bordant when there is a compact oriented $(n+1)$-manifold $W$ with $\partial W=M_0\sqcup(-M_1)$ and a map $F:W\to X$ restricting to $f_0$ and $f_1$ on the boundary. Disjoint union defines the operation. For a group $G$, $K(G,1)$ denotes a connected CW space with fundamental group $G$ and contractible universal cover.

For every path-connected CW space $X$, disjoint union makes $\Omega_n^{SO}(X)$ an abelian group with identity the empty manifold with its unique map to $X$ and inverse of $(M,f)$ represented by $(-M,f)$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: Put $F=\mathbb C(t)$. For any smooth four-manifold $V$ over $B$ let $D(V)$ be its twisted nonsingular image Witt form minus the scalar extension to $F$ of its ordinary complex nonsingular image form. The representation $(a,n)\mapsto\zeta_d^at^n$ is unitary for the stipulated involution. By [F3], the two terms vanish on a closed five-bordism boundary with their respective extending systems. Hence on closed four-manifolds their difference is a homomorphism from $\Omega_4^{SO}(B)$ to $W(F)$. For a constant map the two coefficient systems are the same constant $F$ system, so $D(Z,\mathrm{constant})=0$.

Applying that homomorphism to [F2] gives $dD(Z,f)=0$ for every closed $Z$ over $B$. In particular every closed ambiguity has torsion Witt difference and becomes zero after tensoring with $\mathbb Q$. This conclusion concerns the entire Witt class, not just its signature. No arbitrary-group analytic index theorem is required.

If the bounding multiplicities are $r_0,r_1$, take $r_1$ disjoint copies of $W_0$ and $r_0$ copies of $W_1$. Their whole marked boundaries are the same $r_0r_1$ copies. Glue them, reversing the second orientation, with the same boundary character maps. Whole-boundary Witt gluing [F3] gives $$D(Z)=r_1D(W_0)-r_0D(W_1).$$ This uses the ordinary nonsingular quotient even when the ordinary absolute form has a radical. The twisted boundary is acyclic by [F1], so that term uses precisely the absolute module of the Statement. By step 2.1 the left side is zero rationally. Dividing by $r_0r_1$ proves $D(W_0)/r_0=D(W_1)/r_1$. Disjoint union, repeated multiples and all marked gluing choices are therefore compatible.

We also record the target enlargement needed for a disk extension. Embed $C_d$ in $C_D$ for $d\mid D$ by $a\mapsto(D/d)a$, and keep the infinite coordinate unchanged. With positive roots of unity, $\zeta_D^{(D/d)a}=\zeta_d^a$, so the two rank-one $F$ coefficient systems and their forms are literally the same. Regard any original bounding datum as a datum over the larger target. Even if its boundary map is not onto that target, the proof of steps 1.1–3.1 still applies: [F2] and [F3] allow arbitrary continuous maps to $B$, and acyclicity concerns the actual coefficient system. One may use the induced principal cover, which can be disconnected; its local coefficient module is unchanged. Thus a smooth filling over the larger finite cyclic target computes the same rational class.

Finally the specified one-sided signature is a well-defined homomorphism on this rational Witt group. The entries of a Hermitian rational matrix, its nonzero determinant, and a rational change-of-basis matrix have only finitely many zeros and poles on the unit circle unless the relevant function is identically zero. For a nonsingular representative choose a short interval $0<\theta<\epsilon$ avoiding those finite exceptional sets. Its evaluations are nonsingular Hermitian matrices, and their eigenvalue signs cannot change without a zero determinant, so the signature is constant there. Congruent representatives have congruent evaluations on a common such interval. A hyperbolic form evaluates to a hyperbolic form and has zero signature. Direct sums add signatures, and rationalization extends this homomorphism by rational linearity. This verifies exactly the one-sided limit specified in the invariant Definition; it does not substitute another averaging convention. Together with step 3.1 this completes the claimed rationalized Witt construction.

citations.quote: Assume AC. Let $D\subset B^4$ be a smooth proper disk, let $p$ be prime, and let $q=p^k$ with $k\ge1$. The $q$-fold cyclic cover $W_{D,q}$ of $B^4$ branched along $D$ is a compact connected oriented $4$-manifold with $H_i(W_{D,q};\mathbb Q)=0$ for every $i>0$ and boundary $\Sigma_q(\partial D)$.

Assume AC. If a smooth oriented knot $K$ bounds a smooth proper disk $D$ in $B^4$ and $q$ is a prime power, then
$$P_D=\ker\bigl(H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)\to H_1(W_{D,q};\mathbb Z)\bigr)$$
is a metabolizer for the torsion linking form of $\Sigma_q(K)$.

Assume AC. Let $D\subset B^4$ be a smooth proper disk with boundary K, let q be a prime power, and let $W_{D,q}$ be its branched cover. Put
$$P_D=\ker\bigl(H_1(\Sigma_q(\partial D);\mathbb Z)\to H_1(W_{D,q};\mathbb Z)\bigr).$$
If $\chi:H_1(\Sigma_q(\partial D);\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$ has prime-power order, then $\chi$ vanishes on $P_D$ if and only if it extends to a character of prime-power order on $H_1(W_{D,q};\mathbb Z)$.

Assume AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot bounding a smooth proper disk $D\subset B^4$, and let $q\ge2$. Write $X_D$ for the compact disk exterior and let the positive meridian induce $\pi_1(X_D)\to H_1(X_D;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z/q$. Let $X_{D,q}$ be the connected cover classified by the kernel of this map. Attach $D^2\times D^2$ to $X_{D,q}$ along the connected cover of $D^2\times S^1$ using the normal-disk map $z\mapsto z^q$. The resulting compact oriented $4$-manifold $W_{D,q}$ is the $q$-fold cyclic cover of $B^4$ branched along $D$; its boundary is $\Sigma_q(K)$, and the local branched model is $(x,z)\mapsto(x,z^q)$.

Assume AC. Let $X_D$ be the exterior of a smooth proper disk, with positive-meridian isomorphism $H_1(X_D;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$. Let $X_{D,\infty}$ be the connected cover classified by the kernel of $\pi_1(X_D)\to H_1(X_D;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$, and let $t$ denote the deck transformation represented by the positive meridian. For $q\ge2$, define $X_{D,q}=X_{D,\infty}/\langle t^q\rangle$.

Let $\mathcal L$ be one local system on $X$.

1. If $Z\subseteq A\subseteq X$ and $\overline Z\subseteq\operatorname{int}_X(A)$, inclusion induces excision isomorphisms in both local homology and local cohomology between $(X\setminus Z,A\setminus Z)$ and $(X,A)$, using the restrictions of $\mathcal L$.
2. For an open cover $X=U\cup V$, there are natural exact sequences
   $$\cdots\to H_n(U\cap V;\mathcal L)\to H_n(U;\mathcal L)\oplus H_n(V;\mathcal L)\to H_n(X;\mathcal L)\to\cdots$$
   and
   $$\cdots\to H^n(X;\mathcal L)\to H^n(U;\mathcal L)\oplus H^n(V;\mathcal L)\to H^n(U\cap V;\mathcal L)\to\cdots,$$
   where all systems are restrictions and the middle difference map in cohomology is $u|_{U\cap V}-v|_{U\cap V}$.

The same conclusions hold for the standard excisive-cover condition after replacing the cover by interiors. A local system given only on a subspace is not silently assumed to extend to $X$.

Assume AC. Let $X$ be a smooth knot exterior or the exterior of a smooth proper disk in the standard four-ball. Its meridian-coordinate homomorphism is $\ell:\pi_1X\to\mathbb Z$. Let $X_q$ be its connected $q$-fold cyclic cover, for any $q\ge1$, and put $\psi=\ell/q$ on its group. For any homomorphism $c:\pi_1X_q\to C_{p^a}$, where $p$ is prime and $a\ge1$, give $\mathbb C(t)$ the rank-one unitary coefficient system
$$\rho(g)=\zeta_{p^a}^{c(g)}t^{\psi(g)},\qquad \bar t=t^{-1}.$$
Then $H_*(X_q;\mathbb C(t)_\rho)=0$. The same conclusion holds for a trivial finite character.

If $M_{0,q}$ is the $q$-fold cover of zero surgery on a smooth knot, and $c$ is any prime-power-order character on its first homology, the same conclusion holds on $M_{0,q}$ with its meridian free coordinate. In particular every smooth four-bordism whose boundary consists of such data has a nonsingular twisted middle Hermitian form, with no change to its absolute twisted $H_2$. The regular $C_{p^a}\times\mathbb Z$ cover in this assertion is generally infinite; the assertion concerns its specified rank-one localization.

Assume AC. For a fixed prime-power cover degree and prime-power order character, the rationalized difference between the twisted and untwisted Casson–Gordon intersection-form Witt classes, divided by the bounding multiplicity $r$, is independent of the chosen multiple and bounding pair. It defines a class in $W(\mathbb C(t))\otimes\mathbb Q$.

Assume AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $q$ be a prime power, and let $\chi:H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$ have prime-power order $d$. Choose a Casson–Gordon bordism datum $(M_{0,q},\eta,r,W)$. Write $G=\mathbb Z/d\oplus\mathbb Z$, let $Y\to W$ be the regular cover determined by $\eta$, and give $\mathbb C(t)$ the $G$-action $(a,n)z=\exp(2\pi ia/d)t^n z$ and involution $\overline{t}=t^{-1}$ with complex conjugation on constants. Define
$$H_2^t(W;\mathbb C)=H_2(Y;\mathbb C)\otimes_{\mathbb C[G]}\mathbb C(t).$$
The Casson–Gordon Witt class is
$$\tau(\Sigma_q(K),\chi)=\frac{1}{r}\bigl([H_2^t(W;\mathbb C)]-[Q_0(W)\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C(t)]\bigr)\in W(\mathbb C(t))\otimes\mathbb Q,$$
using the nonsingular twisted form and the ordinary nonsingular image form. Precisely, put $Q_0(W)=H_2(W;\mathbb C)/\operatorname{rad}(\lambda_W)$ with its induced form; the untwisted term in the display is understood as $Q_0(W)\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C(t)$. The twisted boundary complex is acyclic, so its algebraic Poincare cap preserves the absolute twisted module. This does not assert that an arbitrary ordinary absolute intersection form is nonsingular. Here $W(\mathbb C(t))$ is the Witt group of nonsingular Hermitian forms over the field with involution, modulo hyperbolic forms. Its signature defect is $\sigma(K,\chi)=\sigma_1(\tau(\Sigma_q(K),\chi))$, where $\sigma_1$ evaluates a Hermitian representative at $t=e^{i\theta}$ and takes the one-sided limit as $\theta\to0^+$. This is the specified Casson–Gordon invariant and signature homomorphism; it is not an arbitrary rho invariant or an unspecified difference of signatures.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere and let $B^4$ be the standard four-ball with boundary $S^3$. Let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable smooth properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. Let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable locally flat topologically properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. For each such surface, its genus $g(F)$ is the nonnegative integer determined by $\chi(F)=1-2g(F)$. Define the smooth slice genus and the locally flat topological slice genus by

$$
g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K):=\min\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K),\qquad g_4^{\mathrm{top}}(K):=\min\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K).
$$

derivations.claim: By [F1], choose an extending character $\widetilde\chi$ on the branched disk cover, and write its exact order as $D=p^a$. If the original nontrivial character has order $d=p^b$, then $d\mid D$. Restrict $\widetilde\chi$ to $H_1(X_{D,q})$ and pair it with $\ell/q$. Its finite coordinate vanishes on the lifted meridian because that circle bounds the branch-tube disk in the filled cover. Its infinite coordinate takes that circle to one. On the exterior of the boundary knot the finite coordinate is the original $\chi$; on the zero-filling solid torus it is zero. Thus its boundary is precisely the original $\eta$ followed by the inclusion $C_d\times\mathbb Z\to C_D\times\mathbb Z$, with the root representation unchanged.

The actual oriented boundary of $X_{D,q}$ is $M_{0,q}$. Indeed the product disk tube at the base disk gives a longitude filling of the knot exterior: its framing is zero, since a parallel disk is disjoint and its boundary has linking zero with $K$. Passing to the meridional $q$-cover lifts the same longitude slope, while its normal circle is the closed lift of $\mu^q$. These are the zero-surgery cover coordinates in [F2], with the positive boundary orientation retained. Mayer–Vietoris in the rational homology ball $W_{D,q}=X_{D,q}\cup(D^2\times D^2)$, whose overlap is $D^2\times S^1$, gives $H_2(X_{D,q};\mathbb Q)=0$ and $H_1(X_{D,q};\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$ on that overlap circle. The higher groups vanish as well. In particular its ordinary middle nonsingular image form is zero.

The character in step 1.1 is of prime-power order on the actual exterior cover. Hence [F3] gives $H_2(X_{D,q};\mathbb C(t))=0$, so its twisted form is also zero. The difference of the two Witt forms of this actual single-boundary smooth filling is therefore zero. By [F4]'s larger-target comparison it computes the original rationalized class even when $D>d$: compare any original multiple bounding datum, viewed over $C_D\times\mathbb Z$, with the same number of copies of this filling and use the closed fourth-bordism ambiguity calculation. The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $F$ be a connected compact oriented Seifert surface of genus $g$, and let $V$ be its positive-push Seifert matrix in an ordered integral basis of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$. Write $\Delta_K(t)$ for the Alexander polynomial normalized up to multiplication by $\pm t^k$, and let $q\ge2$ with $\zeta_q$ a primitive $q$-th root of unity. Then $H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)$ is finite if and only if $\Delta_K(\zeta_q^j)\ne0$ for every $1\le j<q$, and, when it is finite,
$$
|H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)|=\prod_{j=1}^{q-1}|\Delta_K(\zeta_q^j)|.
$$
The same criterion and order hold when $\Delta_K(t)$ is replaced by $\det(V-tV^T)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented embedded circle in the oriented standard three-sphere, let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with boundary $K$, and let $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ be any ordered integral basis of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ with Seifert matrix $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. Let $J_F$ be the matrix of the algebraic intersection form on $F$, with a transverse intersection of oriented curves $u,v$ counted positively exactly when their ordered tangent vectors form a positive basis of $TF$. Then $V-V^T=J_F$. The matrix $J_F$ is skew-symmetric and unimodular; when $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ is a standard handle basis, it is a direct sum of blocks $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}$.

For every $n\ge1$ the cyclotomic polynomial $\Phi_n$
([[def-cyclotomic-polynomial]]) is irreducible in $\mathbb Q[t]$
([[def-irreducible-and-prime-elements-in-a-domain]]).

Assume AC. If $Y$ is a closed connected oriented $3$-manifold with finite $H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)$, then the bounding-chain torsion linking pairing $\lambda_Y$ is symmetric and nonsingular: its adjoint $H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H_1(Y;\mathbb Z),\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$ is an isomorphism.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $R$ be a PID, $C$ a chain complex of free
right $R$-modules, and $G$ a left $R$-module. Then naturally in $C,G$,
$0\to H_n(C)\otimes_RG\to H_n(C\otimes_RG)\to\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(H_{n-1}(C),G)\to0$
is exact.

Assume AC. Let $M$ be an $R$-oriented boundaryless $n$-manifold, with $R$ commutative unital; manifolds are Hausdorff and second countable here. Then cap with the compatible compact orientation classes gives isomorphisms
$$D_M:H_c^p(M;R)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{n-p}(M;R)$$
for every integer $p$, including disconnected, noncompact and empty $M$.

Naturality means that for an open inclusion $i:U\hookrightarrow M$ with restricted orientation, $D_M e=i_*D_U$, where $e$ is extension of compact supports. For compact $M$, $H_c^p(M;R)=H^p(M;R)$ canonically and $D_M(a)=a\cap[M]$. For arbitrary $M$ the isomorphism is the direct sum of those on its components. AC is used in the countable coordinate-neighborhood selection for exhaustion and in the local universal-coefficient proof.

derivations.claim: Suppose a nontrivial $q$-th root of unity $\omega$ were a zero of $D$. Its order is $p^s$ for some $1\le s\le k$. By [F3], the minimal polynomial $\Phi_{p^s}$ divides $D$ in $\mathbb Q[t]$. Since $\Phi_{p^s}$ is monic and both polynomials have integer coefficients, polynomial long division gives an integer-coefficient quotient with zero remainder. Thus $p=\Phi_{p^s}(1)$ divides $D(1)$.
This contradicts $D(1)=\pm1$ from [F2]. Therefore $D$ has no zero at any nontrivial $q$-th root of unity. The criterion [F1] gives finiteness of $H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)$.
By [F5], the finite first homology from step 2.1 makes $\Sigma_q(K)$ a rational homology sphere. Its torsion linking form is nonsingular by [F4], which proves the final assertion.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $q=p^k$ for a prime $p$ and $k\ge1$. Then $H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)$ is finite, so $\Sigma_q(K)$ is a rational homology sphere and carries a nonsingular torsion linking form.

Assume AC. If a smooth oriented knot $K$ bounds a smooth proper disk $D$ in $B^4$ and $q$ is a prime power, then
$$P_D=\ker\bigl(H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)\to H_1(W_{D,q};\mathbb Z)\bigr)$$
is a metabolizer for the torsion linking form of $\Sigma_q(K)$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere and let $B^4$ be the standard four-ball with boundary $S^3$. Let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable smooth properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. Let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable locally flat topologically properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. For each such surface, its genus $g(F)$ is the nonnegative integer determined by $\chi(F)=1-2g(F)$. Define the smooth slice genus and the locally flat topological slice genus by

$$
g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K):=\min\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K),\qquad g_4^{\mathrm{top}}(K):=\min\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K).
$$

A finite nonsingular linking form is a pair $(A,\lambda)$, where $A$ is a finite abelian group and $\lambda:A\times A\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$ is symmetric and induces an isomorphism $A\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$. For $P\le A$, put $P^\perp=\{a\in A:\lambda(a,p)=0\text{ for every }p\in P\}$. A metabolizer is a subgroup $P$ with $P=P^\perp$; equivalently, $\lambda$ vanishes on $P\times P$ and $|P|^2=|A|$.

Assume AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $q\ge2$, and let $M=\Sigma_q(K)$ be its $q$-fold cyclic branched cover. A character is a homomorphism $\chi:H_1(M;\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$. Its order is its order in $\operatorname{Hom}(H_1(M;\mathbb Z),\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$; it is finite-order when this order is finite and has prime-power order when its order is $p^e$ for a prime $p$ and $e\ge1$. It vanishes on a subgroup $P$ when $\chi(x)=0$ for every $x\in P$.

Assume AC. Let $K$ be a smooth slice knot, let $q$ be a prime power, let $D$ be a smooth slice disk, and let $P_D$ be the induced metabolizer in $H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)$. For every prime-power-order character $\chi:H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$ that vanishes on $P_D$, the Casson–Gordon signature defect $\sigma(K,\chi)$ is zero.

derivations.claim: Prove the contrapositive. Suppose $K$ is smoothly slice, and choose its smooth proper disk $D$. By [F1] its prime-power branched-cover first homology is finite, and by [F2] the disk kernel $P_D$ is a metabolizer of its nonsingular linking form.

Every prime-power-order character vanishing on this particular $P_D$ has $\sigma(K,\chi)=0$ by the now proved vanishing statement [F6]. Therefore the universal metabolizer hypothesis in the Statement fails at $P_D$: there is no such character with nonzero defect. We have proved that smooth sliceness implies the negation of that hypothesis, so contraposition gives the stated obstruction. If the linking form has no metabolizer, smooth sliceness already contradicts [F2]; no independent existence of a metabolizer was assumed. All prime-power quantifiers and the stated smooth and AC scope are retained.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the full Axiom of Choice. A positive Hopf band is an oriented annulus whose two boundary components, with their induced orientations, have linking number $+1$. Let $F$ be the genus-one Seifert surface obtained by plumbing two positive Hopf bands in a square, with oriented core curves $a,b$ forming a positive handle basis, and choose the plumbing side so that $a^+$ bounds a disk in $S^3$ disjoint from $b$. The oriented boundary of this standard positive two-band plumbing is the right-handed trefoil. In the positive-push convention $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$ with ordered basis $(a,b)$, the Seifert matrix is
$$
V=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\-1&-1\end{pmatrix}.
$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ bound a connected compact oriented Seifert surface $F$ of genus $g$. Choose a disk-band decomposition of $F$ with one disk and $2g$ bands, and use its band-core basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ to form the positive-push Seifert matrix $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. For $q\ge2$, define the symmetric block matrix $M_q(V)$ of size $2g(q-1)$ by specifying its $2g\times2g$ blocks, indexed by $1\le k,\ell\le q-1$:
$$(M_q(V))_{k\ell}=\begin{cases}V+V^T,&k=\ell,\\-V^T,&\ell=k+1,\\-V,&k=\ell+1,\\0,&|k-\ell|\ge2.\end{cases}$$
Push the interior of $F$ into $B^4$ while keeping $K$ on $S^3=\partial B^4$, cut $B^4$ along a thickened copy of the pushed-in surface, and take $q$ copies. For $i=1,\ldots,q-1$, glue the positive face of copy $i$ to the negative face of copy $i+1$ by reflecting the normal coordinate; do not glue the last positive face to the first negative face. Call the resulting $q$-fold cyclic branched cover $W_q(F)$. It has one $0$-handle and $2g(q-1)$ $2$-handles, and its framed attaching link has linking matrix $M_q(V)$. The boundary branched cover, with the boundary marking induced by the covering map, is $\Sigma_q(K)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $J=J_1\cup\cdots\cup J_n$ be an oriented link of $n\ge1$ smooth components in $S^3$. Choose pairwise disjoint closed tubular neighborhoods $N(J_i)$, let $X=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}(\bigcup_iN(J_i))$, and let $\mu_i$ be the positive meridian of $J_i$. Let $\lambda_i$ be the longitude parallel to $J_i$ with zero self-linking. Alexander duality identifies $H_1(X;\mathbb Z)$ with $\mathbb Z^n$ on the meridian basis $[\mu_1],\ldots,[\mu_n]$; for $i\ne j$, define $\operatorname{lk}_{S^3}(J_i,J_j)$ to be the $j$-th coordinate of $[\lambda_i]$, the usual oriented linking number. Use the boundary-torus intersection convention $\mu_i\mathbin{\cdot}\lambda_i=+1$. Give $J_i$ an integer framing $f_i$ and fill along $\delta_i=\lambda_i+f_i\mu_i$. Let $A$ be the symmetric integer matrix with $A_{ii}=f_i$ and $A_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}_{S^3}(J_i,J_j)$ for $i\ne j$. Assume $\det A\ne0$, and let $Y$ be the resulting oriented surgery manifold, oriented as the boundary of the 4-dimensional surgery handlebody with outward normal first. Then $H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^n/A\mathbb Z^n$. For torsion classes $[C],[D]\in H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)$ represented by oriented 1-cycles, choose $m>0$ and an integral 2-chain $F$ with $\partial F=mC$ and define $\lambda_Y([C],[D])=(F\mathbin{\cdot}D)/m\pmod{\mathbb Z}$, where the intersection is signed by the orientation of $Y$. If $x,y\in\mathbb Z^n$ are meridian-coordinate representatives of $[C],[D]$, then
$$
\lambda_Y([x],[y])=-x^TA^{-1}y\pmod{\mathbb Z}.
$$

A finite nonsingular linking form is a pair $(A,\lambda)$, where $A$ is a finite abelian group and $\lambda:A\times A\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$ is symmetric and induces an isomorphism $A\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$. For $P\le A$, put $P^\perp=\{a\in A:\lambda(a,p)=0\text{ for every }p\in P\}$. A metabolizer is a subgroup $P$ with $P=P^\perp$; equivalently, $\lambda$ vanishes on $P\times P$ and $|P|^2=|A|$.

Let $Y$ be a closed oriented $3$-manifold and let $x,y\in\operatorname{Tor}H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)$. Choose integral $1$-cycles $a,b$ representing $x,y$, respectively. For choices of an integer $n>0$ and an integral $2$-chain $C$ with $\partial C=na$, the bounding-chain expression is $(C\cdot b)/n\bmod\mathbb Z\in\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$, where $C$ and $b$ are placed transversely and intersection signs use the orientation of $Y$. This expression is the torsion linking pairing when its independence of the choices is established.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $J=J_1\cup\cdots\cup J_n$ be an oriented link of $n\ge1$ smooth components in $S^3$. Choose pairwise disjoint closed tubular neighborhoods $N(J_i)$, let $X=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}(\bigcup_iN(J_i))$, and let $\mu_i$ be the positive meridian of $J_i$. Let $\lambda_i$ be the longitude parallel to $J_i$ with zero self-linking. Alexander duality identifies $H_1(X;\mathbb Z)$ with $\mathbb Z^n$ on the meridian basis $[\mu_1],\ldots,[\mu_n]$; for $i\ne j$, define $\operatorname{lk}_{S^3}(J_i,J_j)$ to be the $j$-th coordinate of $[\lambda_i]$, the usual oriented linking number. Use the boundary-torus intersection convention $\mu_i\mathbin{\cdot}\lambda_i=+1$. Give $J_i$ an integer framing $f_i$ and fill along $\delta_i=\lambda_i+f_i\mu_i$. Let $A$ be the symmetric integer matrix with $A_{ii}=f_i$ and $A_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}_{S^3}(J_i,J_j)$ for $i\ne j$. Assume $\det A\ne0$, and let $Y$ be the resulting oriented surgery manifold, oriented as the boundary of the 4-dimensional surgery handlebody with outward normal first. Then $H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^n/A\mathbb Z^n$. For torsion classes $[C],[D]\in H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)$ represented by oriented 1-cycles, choose $m>0$ and an integral 2-chain $F$ with $\partial F=mC$ and define $\lambda_Y([C],[D])=(F\mathbin{\cdot}D)/m\pmod{\mathbb Z}$, where the intersection is signed by the orientation of $Y$. If $x,y\in\mathbb Z^n$ are meridian-coordinate representatives of $[C],[D]$, then
$$
\lambda_Y([x],[y])=-x^TA^{-1}y\pmod{\mathbb Z}.
$$

Assume AC. If $Y$ is a closed connected oriented $3$-manifold with finite $H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)$, then the bounding-chain torsion linking pairing $\lambda_Y$ is symmetric and nonsingular: its adjoint $H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H_1(Y;\mathbb Z),\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$ is an isomorphism.
